comment: `ConsoleLineEdit.__init__` still calls `stylesheet.set_register(self)`, but this patch removes the class's `STYLESHEET`. Please remove that registration as well (the parent `ConsoleWidget` now owns the console font stylesheet), otherwise registration may fail or unexpectedly register an inherited stylesheet.

`host` is now converted to native `str` unconditionally. If `self._r.url` is a bytes URL, `urlparse()` returns byte components, so `urlunparse()` will receive a `str` host mixed with bytes and raise `TypeError`. The previous conditional intentionally retained a bytes host in that case. Please either preserve the host type based on the parsed URL or ensure the URL is normalized before reconstruction, and add coverage for a bytes URL with a bytes `Host` header.

Removing the copy makes `result` alias `reply.result`, so serializing `result[DATA]` now also changes the client reply for `SCHEMA` and `ISSUER_KEY` from structured data to a JSON string. Please preserve the response representation (for example, serialize a copy only for ledger persistence) and normalize the graph-replay path separately if that is the inconsistency being fixed.

Keep validating `build_directory` after `setup_build()`. A truthy setup result does not itself guarantee that `BUILD_DIR` is populated, and this change can pass `None` into `Runner`, deferring the failure or causing unexpected behavior. For example: `if not build_setup_result or not build_directory: raise CorpusPruningException(...)`.
Please change this message to "Unable to send inventory summary email"; this notifier does not send violation emails, so the current exception log is misleading during diagnosis.

The new format string opens `(` before `CP` but never closes it, so emitted encounter messages end with output like `NCP: 85.0` instead of `NCP: 85.0)`. Add the closing `)` after the final placeholder.

`next_ocurrance` is misspelled; the correct spelling is `next_occurrence`, which was the previous method name. Renaming this method to the misspelled form can break existing references to `self.next_occurrence` and appears contrary to the PR's stated intent.

`HISTORY.rst`: The new entry says invalid-header errors “now include the header name,” but the replaced message already included `name` via `"Header %s value %s..."`. Please describe the actual formatting change instead, or clarify what behavior this PR is intended to add.

In `check_header_validity`, could this be formatted as `{%s: %s}`? Without a space after the colon, values such as lists or dictionaries run into the header name and make the diagnostic harder to scan.

Removing the early `setWindowFlags` call means `_set_decoration` now runs near the end of `__init__`, after window geometry has been initialized. Qt's `setWindowFlags()` can reset a top-level window's position when it reparents the widget, so this can discard the restored/requested geometry (and now happens even when `hide_decoration` is false). Apply the initial flags before geometry initialization, and reserve the late call for runtime changes.
In `BgzfReader.readline`, “for the BGZF file” is awkward and suggests purpose rather than source. Please use “Read a single line from the BGZF file.”

In the new-agent branch, assign the result of `explode_agents()` back to `agent`. The initial lookup entered this branch because it was empty, so discarding the fetched result leaves `agent[0]` below raising `IndexError` on every first heartbeat from a new agent.

The inline comment is redundant—it restates the already evident use of `itemgetter` without explaining what alternative it outperforms. Please remove it or document the specific performance rationale; if retained, use two spaces before the inline `#` per the surrounding style.

`TypeSlots.special_method_names` is built as `set(get_slot_table(...))`, but `SlotTable.__iter__()` yields slot descriptor objects, not method-name strings. Therefore `attr_name in TypeSlots.special_method_names` will always be false for names such as `__add__`, preventing dispatch to the corresponding `slot__...` handler. Please build this set from the `method_name_to_slot` keys (or expose a membership API on `SlotTable`).

`_key()` reintroduces `six.u(...)`, but this PR removes both `luigi.six.u` and the `six` import from this module. The `unbatched_params` path will therefore fail with an undefined name or missing attribute. Use native string literals and `str.format()`, as intended by the PR.
Please use an imperative summary, e.g. `"""Ensure that gradients can be computed."""`, rather than the gerund phrase “Making sure…”.

Place `# doctest: +IGNORE_EXCEPTION_DETAIL` on the `>>> obj.unwrap(...)` line (or on a `...` continuation line). In its current position it is parsed as expected output rather than source, so the directive is not applied and the doctest will fail.
Please fix the spelling errors in this comment: `pipline's` should be `pipeline's`, and `unmmaped` should be `unmapped`.

`graph` is a read-only property backed by `self._graph`, so assigning `self.graph = ...` in `process()` will raise `AttributeError`. Keep assigning to `self._graph`, or explicitly add a setter/change the property before using `self.graph` as storage.
Please retain a space after `#` (`# insert detail info about gym to fort`) to follow standard Python comment formatting and preserve readability.

Please keep `ERROR_PROBABILITY` (or update all consumers as part of this change). The Kinesis throttling/error-injection logic in `localstack/mock/infra.py` relies on this constant to determine when to return an error, so removing it from `constants.py` leaves that path with an undefined name at runtime.

`scheduling_seed` should also be annotated as `Optional[int]`. Like `seed`, it is forwarded to the `seed` argument of a stateful TensorFlow random operation (`bernoulli_sample`), which expects a Python integer; `TensorLike` lets `@typechecked` accept tensors that will fail downstream.

Calling `setup_test_logging()` at module import time installs handlers on the process-wide root logger. Since `CLI.setup_logging` is no longer guarded by `@run_once`, later CLI construction can add another set of handlers, causing duplicate output and leaving the bootstrap file handler open across tests. Please avoid this import-time setup or explicitly tear down/remove the handlers before normal CLI setup.
Please fix the typos in the reformatted comment: “seperate” should be “separate”, and “One for for” should be “One for”.

The new assertion requires every image in the batch to have at least one RoI. In a mixed batch where one image has no predicted/truth boxes but another does, `rois` is non-empty so the cascade-level `len(rois) == 0` guard will not apply, and this assertion will terminate training. `refine_bboxes` should instead handle a missing image ID by appending an empty bbox tensor for that image.

`check_symbols_cached` expects the path to the `.cached_build_params` file, but this call passes `symbols_directory`. Construct `os.path.join(symbols_directory, '.cached_build_params')` and pass that instead; otherwise the cache file is never read (and attempting to read a directory may also fail), so locally available symbols will not trigger the early return.

`_update_auth_constraint()` still accesses `self._update_state_by_versions`, but this initialization is now removed. Any normal auth-rule state update through this handler will raise `AttributeError`; either retain the initialization or update `_update_auth_constraint()` to use the new versioned-handler dispatch exclusively.
Remove `is_linux` from `from bzt.utils import get_full_path, is_linux`; after dropping the platform guard, it is no longer used in this file.

Since `ValueError` is generic, please add `match=` for the expected validation message to each `pytest.raises` call. Otherwise an unrelated `ValueError` from selection, slicing, or analysis could make these regression tests pass without exercising the intended finish/begin-time checks.

`RestService` already defines `update_config`, and this later definition overrides it. In particular, it bypasses the existing plugin-specific update logic shown in the related hunk, so plugin configuration updates will no longer perform that behavior. Please extend/consolidate the existing method rather than redefining it.

`cross_valid` is now ignored in `__len__`. When it is enabled, the dataset should presumably expose the complement of the selected fold for cross-validation training, not the selected fold's size. Please implement the cross-validation length/indexing semantics (or remove the option) rather than returning the same length for both modes.

This conditional rewrite is behaviorally equivalent to the previous code: truthy `background` still emits `tab_index_changed`, while falsy `background` still calls `setCurrentWidget(tab)`. As written, the patch does not change when the status-bar update occurs, so it does not appear to fix #1247. Is an additional emission or different condition needed?

`plugin_path[1]` only works when `plugins` is the first path component. For an absolute path or a prefixed relative path such as `/app/plugins/stockpile/...` or `app/plugins/stockpile/...`, this records the wrong component as the plugin. Derive the name relative to the actual `plugins` component (for example, `plugin_path[plugin_path.index('plugins') + 1]`) and guard against a missing following component.

Please retain the `torch.__version__ < '1.3'` branch alongside the new Parrots check. Removing it means BatchNorm modules on supported legacy PyTorch versions are no longer wrapped to cast half-precision inputs to float, potentially causing FP16 execution failures there.

`kwargs['colors'] = kwargs.pop('bbox_color', 'green')` now overwrites an explicitly supplied `colors` argument whenever `bbox_color` is absent. Previously, `colors` passed through unchanged. Please preserve an existing `colors` value, e.g. only set the default when neither argument is present.

The docstring hard-codes “12 hours” even though the threshold is defined by `TIME_TO_CONSIDER_STATS_AS_OLD`. Refer to the configured constant generically so the documentation does not become stale when the value changes.

Removing `Proxy.__repr__` drops the proxy-specific `valid_values` representation and makes `Proxy` fall back to its inherited representation. Is this intentional? It appears contrary to the PR’s stated goal of adding representations for config types and may regress diagnostic/debug output for this type.

Renaming this function to `layer_test_esn` prevents pytest from discovering it because its name no longer starts with `test_`. Please use a discoverable name such as `test_esn_layer`; otherwise the layer behavior and dtype coverage in this function will not run.
